## ⛔ Escalation — the hazard is worse than filed. The un-drafting is not reliably reversible, and this one merged.

`domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (objectstack-ai/objectui#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`, 2026-08-25. The card above described a recoverable mistake. It was not recovered.

### What the original filing got wrong

It said the PR "was converted back to draft and did not land". Both halves were true when written and the second stopped being true minutes later:

| time | event |
|:--|:--|
| ~12:11Z | `update_pull_request(reviewers: [...])` on a draft PR → `draft: false` |
| ~12:31Z | PR enters objectui's **merge queue** |
| 12:45:44Z | converted back to **draft**; `origin/main` verified not to contain it |
| ~12:5xZ | ⛔ **the queue merged it anyway** — `5b3290fd5` on `main` |

### The second fact, and it is the dangerous one

⭐ **Converting a pull request to draft does NOT remove it from a merge queue it has already entered.** The entry keeps its position and merges on schedule. `disable_pr_auto_merge` is also unavailable at that point — it returns `Can't disable auto-merge for this pull request`.

So the failure mode is not "a tool call publishes a draft", which a careful seat could notice and undo. It is:

> a tool call publishes a draft → the queue accepts it → **neither of the two obvious remedies works** → it merges without a human, on a surface whose entire protection is that a human merges it.

The window between the mistaken call and the merge was about **forty minutes**, and both attempted remedies inside that window failed. A seat that noticed even faster than I did would still have needed to know that "dequeue" is a distinct operation from "convert to draft" — which is exactly the knowledge this fact table exists to carry.

### What this changes about the dispositions

Disposition 1 (a fact-table line) now needs **two** lines, and the second matters more:

1. `update_pull_request` sends `draft` even when omitted, so any call against a draft PR must pass `draft: true` explicitly.
2. ⛔ **Once a PR is in a merge queue, converting it to draft does not dequeue it, and `disable_pr_auto_merge` refuses.** Do not report a mistaken publish as remediated on the strength of either. Establish that a real dequeue path exists — and that it worked — before saying so.

Disposition 2 (skill text) gains urgency: the ACCEPT-path fork tells seats to request review on a governed-surface draft, which is the call that triggers this. That instruction is unsafe as written and should carry `draft: true` inline.

⚠️ A third disposition, new: the seat-discipline defence has now demonstrably failed once. Worth deciding whether governed paths should carry a **machine** gate (required review / CODEOWNERS on `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `docs/adr/**`) so the next occurrence cannot merge regardless of which tool misbehaves. That is a maintainer decision, filed as objectstack-ai/objectui#6325 option C.

### Consequence on record

objectui `AGENTS.md` on `main` carries a change no human merged. Keep-or-revert is with the maintainer as objectstack-ai/objectui#6325, with the incident timeline on objectstack-ai/objectui#6183. ⛔ Not reverted unilaterally: a revert of `AGENTS.md` is itself a governed-surface change and would repeat the violation in the opposite direction.

Scope, per the card's dispositions with the rule stated over the WHOLE tool: (1) platform-readings fact line — `update_pull_request` sends `draft` whether or not the caller supplies it; any call against a draft PR (reviewers, title, body, labels, anything) must pass `draft: true` explicitly; (2) the SKILL.md ACCEPT-path fork's "request review `os-zhuang`" instruction carries the `draft: true` requirement inline at the point of use — a fact-table line alone is not read at the moment of the call; (3) the implementer measures whether a dedicated review-request path exists that does not carry the `draft` field before hardening around the general-purpose updater. ⚠️ Serial: the SKILL.md main file is held in-flight by #12212 (this seat's dispatch); this card queues behind it.
